svg.title: Ledger: the status of 38 claims and results, as the record stands
svg.desc: A list of 38 claims and results with their status: 10 established, 2 refuted, 3 contested, 12 unclear, 2 inconclusive under a rule set before the run, 9 not yet checkable. None of the four claims is established or refuted.
svg.text: Ledger: the status of 38 claims and results, as the record stands
One square per claim or result, grouped by section: the note's four claims, its rivals and its evidence items, then checks on the
data from the repository's records. Every status has a glyph as well as a colour, and every row cites its basis in the table.
Inconclusive under a rule set before the run
Claim A: enacting the 2023 package would put at imminent risk the right to vote, equal citizenship and a
Claim B: losing those protections is an imminent threat to the state itself
Claim C: the Court's doctrine is not a device for preserving a liberal elite's hegemony
Claim D, the project's own: Capability × Intent adequately describes the threat
R1: narrow self-interest rather than identity change
R2: good-faith rebalancing of an activist court
R5, strong form: the Court intervenes only against enactments that narrow the judiciary
R5, weak form: a higher intervention rate against enactments that narrow the judiciary
The elite-hegemony thesis (Hirschl; Gavison; Medina, fn. 4), as this project operationalizes it
Comparative base rate: backsliding elsewhere ended in weaker democracies, not vanished states (Bermeo,
The product form is adequate: capability net of resistance captures everything
The full 2023 plan was not enacted. Medina attributes the setback to the protests, which mobilized
foreign governments, business and reservists (pp. 686-687), and says the October 7, 2023 attack and the
war that followed halted the plan (p. 687)
Medina: the two 2023 amendments were both coalition-only and took immediate effect (p. 687)
The Court struck the Reasonableness amendment and deferred the Incapacity amendment to the next Knesset
Medina: Hasson (2021) declared the identity limit but avoided applying it, using interpretation (p. 698)
Resler (1977): Medina's reading set against the Court's own later account
Medina: in the early decades a bipartisan tradition mitigated the simple-majority power to amend; in
recent years, especially since the government elected at the end of 2022, it has been exploited (p. 708)
The government returned to the plan in 2025 (Medina, p. 687)
Nothing in the paper tests a mechanism of the chain from regime loss to state loss
After the article's cut-off: the 2025 amendment has deferred effect; the Court held the Shin Bet chief's
dismissal unlawful after the government had rescinded it, froze and then annulled the attorney general's
dismissal, and in May 2026 ordered the selection committee convened
Medina: the Knesset increasingly exploited the amendment power in recent years, from the past decade,
especially since late 2022 (pp. 696, 707, 708); the 2016, 2018 and 2020 rows carry abuse signs
The full list of 130 laws titled Basic Law, 1958 to 2026, corrected for the merge defect: after the
split, every law of the list as first built is accounted for, and none appears twice
The full list's completeness, compared with the Court's count of 139 changes to 2023
The figure of 141 Basic-Law changes to January 2023
All 39 sampled laws: no challenge found in the searches made
3 of the sampled laws still need a court-database check
One final vote per law: 18 sampled laws whose found vote approved that law alone, and no vote shared
The 1980 Jerusalem law: what else its final vote covered
The one-vote expectation on the 20 sampled laws, passed 1959 to 2003, that have no final-reading record
Coders agreed before adjudication on 7 to 9 of the 9 codebook rows for each variable
Coders agreed before adjudication on 34 to 39 of the 39 sampled laws for each variable
The closed list for the situated-beneficiary sign, as first written
The situated-beneficiary sign under the tightened list: a fresh reader met 9 of the 9 expectations
The 1994 override clause's outcome, coded Adverse on the judgment
T1 reaches its six-row minimum only if all five codable rows are discordant
Rule: the ledger lists the note's four claims, its rivals, the results in "What the evidence already says", and the checks run on the data.
Readings and tests are not listed: readings make no claim of their own, and each test's result is listed under the claim it bears on. Statuses
follow the record; quoted wording keeps the sources' strength, and claims are attributed to whoever makes them.
Basis for every row: figures/data/fig6-ledger.csv (from figures/sources/ledger.csv).
